attack_mechanism: CSR operation and write controls are transferred from ID only on a valid, advancing pipeline cycle; halt and deassert-write logic suppress side effects on killed instructions. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.ex_ready` participates in that valid/ready or write-deassert decision before the CSR operation reaches `csr_we_int`; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.ex_ready`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. Forcing `cv32e40p_top.core_i.ex_ready` to preserve the write controls of a killed or halted CSR instruction allows its operation code to reach the CSR block. The supporting RTL chain is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.ex_ready -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. The squashed instruction can assert `csr_we_int` and modify a protected CSR without an architecturally authorized retirement.
